body.statement: Fix \(\mathcal A\) satisfying \(2\le|\mathcal A_i|<\infty\) for every \(i\in V\).  Let \(M_0\) and \(M_1\) be two directly specified SCMs with refinements in \(\mathfrak R(H,L)\), observed alphabets exactly \(\mathcal A\), semi-Markovian roots, time-homogeneous equations, strictly stationary observed laws, and positive finite cylinders.  If \(P_{M_0}(C_{\mathcal A})=P_{M_1}(C_{\mathcal A})\) for every finite cylinder and \(\theta_{M_0}(y;x)\ne\theta_{M_1}(y;x)\), then \(M_0,M_1\in\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A)\), \(P_{M_0}=P_{M_1}\) as measures on \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\), and \(\operatorname{UID}(H,L,\mathcal A,X,Y,\gamma,x,y)=0\).
body.justification: This is now a direct final-model certificate rather than an alphabet-changing lifting theorem.
body.gap: A generic multi-role fixed-alphabet lift remains unavailable.
body.consumer: Sound failure branches must construct final SCMs and then invoke this verifier.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(\mu=P_{M_0}\) and \(\nu=P_{M_1}\). By hypothesis, the refinement of each \(M_j\), \(j\in\{0,1\}\), belongs to \(\mathfrak R(H,L)\). Thus \(\mathrm{def:refinement\text{-}class}\) supplies bounded refinement span, instantaneous acyclicity, and exact summary \(H\). The remaining hypotheses supply the fixed alphabet family \(\mathcal A\), its finiteness and nontriviality, semi-Markovian roots, time-homogeneous structural equations, strict stationarity, and positive finite cylinders. Applying \(\mathrm{def:model\text{-}class}\) gives
\[
 M_0,M_1\in\mathfrak M(H,L,\mathcal A).
\]

We next derive whole-law equality from cylinder equality. Let \(\mathscr E\) be the algebra of finite unions of cylinders in \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\). For any finite collection of cylinders, taking the union of their finite coordinate supports partitions \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\) into finitely many cylinder atoms. Finite additivity and the hypothesis \(\mu(C_{\mathcal A})=\nu(C_{\mathcal A})\) therefore imply
\[
 \mu(E)=\nu(E)\qquad(E\in\mathscr E).
\]
Here is a direct uniqueness argument. Let \(\mathscr D\) be the smallest lambda-system containing \(\mathscr E\). For fixed \(A\in\mathscr E\), the class
\[
 \mathscr D_A=\{B\in\mathscr D:A\cap B\in\mathscr D\}
\]
is a lambda-system containing \(\mathscr E\), because \(\mathscr E\) is an algebra. Hence \(\mathscr D\subseteq\mathscr D_A\). Holding instead \(B\in\mathscr D\) fixed and repeating the same lambda-system argument in the first argument shows that \(A\cap B\in\mathscr D\) for every \(A,B\in\mathscr D\). A lambda-system closed under finite intersections is a sigma-field: complements follow from the lambda-system property, and an arbitrary countable union is converted into a disjoint countable union by successive differences. Consequently
\[
 \mathscr D=\sigma(\mathscr E),
\]
which is the product sigma-field on \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\).

Now define
\[
 \mathscr C=\{B\in\sigma(\mathscr E):
 \mu(A\cap B)=\nu(A\cap B)\text{ for every }A\in\mathscr E\}.
\]
The class \(\mathscr C\) contains \(\Omega_{\mathcal A}\); it is closed under complements because \(\mu(A)=\nu(A)\) for \(A\in\mathscr E\); and it is closed under countable disjoint unions by countable additivity. Thus \(\mathscr C\) is a lambda-system. Since intersections of members of \(\mathscr E\) remain in \(\mathscr E\), equality on \(\mathscr E\) implies \(\mathscr E\subseteq\mathscr C\). Hence \(\mathscr D\subseteq\mathscr C\). Taking \(A=\Omega_{\mathcal A}\in\mathscr E\) yields
\[
 \mu(B)=\nu(B)\qquad(B\in\sigma(\mathscr E)),
\]
so \(P_{M_0}=P_{M_1}\) as measures on the common path space.

Finally, the assumed strict inequality
\[
 \theta_{M_0}(y;x)\neq\theta_{M_1}(y;x)
\]
together with whole-law equality is a counterexample to the implication quantified over compatible model pairs in \(\mathrm{def:uniform\text{-}identification}\). Therefore
\[
 \operatorname{UID}(H,L,\mathcal A,X,Y,\gamma,x,y)=0.
\]
The argument verifies already constructed models on the unchanged alphabets; it performs no alphabet enlargement or model gluing.
